newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tapie appeals six-month jail sentence over yacht.
newsitem.headline: Tapie appeals six-month jail sentence over yacht.

text.p: Bankrupt French business tycoon Bernard Tapie is appealing in the supreme court against a six-month prison sentence for tax fraud over the management of his luxury yacht, justice sources said on Tuesday.
If the challenge, based on a procedural error, is accepted, the June 4 verdict by an appeals court would be annulled and Tapie would be re-tried.

The appeals court had upheld a lower court decision convicting the rags-to-riches ex-cabinet minister for evading more than 12 million francs ($2 million) in taxes by passing off pleasure trips on the Phocea as business expenses.

It had also upheld a 30-month suspended sentence for misusing company funds in underpaying the firm that owned the 74-metre (240-foot) Phocea and was part of his collapsed business empire. Tapie did not challenge that ruling.
He is already serving an eight-month sentence for rigging a soccer match when he was boss of the Marseille soccer club.
The four-masted Phocea, which in Tapie's heyday was the jewel of Marseille's old port, was sold in April to pay off creditors for $6 million, barely half the asking price.
